#2110. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Brugge are just reminding Villa that they are still there. Virgili is at the heart of things again, combining with Vetlesen who works the ball out to Forbs whose cross is well held by Suzuki.

Villa then spring forward, Hemmings breaching the Brugge box, but Buendia’s eventual effort does not make it through a thicket of legs.

Brugge are building with a three-man backline, sending Siquet forward high and wide. They’ve had much of the ball in the opening stages of this half, which is probably part of Villa’s plan. Emery’s side have settled into an out-of-possession 4-4-2.

Vanakan is booked for simulation after going hitting the deck off a challenge from Gomes. There is a knowing smile on the Belgian midfielder’s face which suggests the referee’s convictions were correct.

We are back under way... Siquet replaces Sabbe at the interval.

Nicolas Jackson is off the mark for Aston Villa. He beat Yann Sommer to the ball, held off a defender and was left with the simplest of finishes to round off a fine first half for Villa. pic.twitter.com/gWx6kUTlOX

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson races on to a nothing punt over the top by Torres, and the situation appears under control with two defenders in the striker’s orbit, but Sommer comes steaming out and Jackson nudges the ball past him before sliding it home into a vacant net.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A sloppy Torres pass out from the back goes straight to Vetlesen who picks out Forbs first time. The winger unleashes an effort from range but Suzuki makes a smart stop.

There is a shout for a Villa handball as Virgili prods a cross on to Kamara’s body, but his arms are clearly by his side.

Villa are presented with a great opportunity to break but the pass in behind for Jackson to gallop on to does not have enough juice and the move breaks down. Jackson does have a sight at goal moments later, but he’s only able to poke the ball wide off a free-kick from the right.

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Brugge have certainly not given up the ghost, still looking to work the ball out to Forbs and Virgili on the flanks. Sabbe overlaps down the right but his ball to Vetlesen is cut out and Villa attempt to spring a counter which is snuffed out by Mechele.

Villa midfielder Joao Gomes is having a productive evening as he aims to recover from that nightmare debut.

He was sent off after 40 minutes of his first Villa appearance in the excruciating 4-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Wan-Bissaka drives down the right as Villa look for a third, but his cross is overhit and goes off on the far side. The right intent, though.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 2 (Buendia) Jackson holds up the ball expertly before slipping in Gomes. The midfielder bursts into the box, outwitting Vetlesen before cutting the ball back to an onrushing Buendia who clips the ball past Sommer with aplomb. A crazy couple of minutes!

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 1 (Vetlesen) Brugge are getting a lot of joy down the flanks. This time it is Vetlesen who finds space down the right and he spears a cross into the box. The ball is worked out to the left where the dangerous Virgili sends the ball back into the area and there Vetlesen is to sweep home. The stadium erupts as the Belgian champions restore parity.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

The Jan Breydelstadion had been very noisy but that goal has completely changed the atmosphere.

It is now nervy in the stadium and the Brugge fans are already starting to boo some of their players.

Villa’s first goal of the season and no surprise it comes from their talisman John McGinn.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Goalkeeper Sommer is penalised for handling the ball outside of his box. He had gathered a corner and had stormed forward to set off an attack. He changes his mind mid-throw and attempts to re-catch the ball but ends up wandering outside of his allotted space. The resulting free-kick crashes straight into the wall.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. He offloads the ball to McGinn on the right of the area and the Scotsman steadies himself before curling the ball into the far post, beyond Sommer.

It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

The £30m signing from Parma possesses a wide passing range and much of Villa’s build-up play starts with the Japan international.

He is Villa’s very own version of Manchester City’s former pass master Ederson.

Much has been made of Suzuki’s distribution and he has already teased a couple of lovely flighted balls up-field. Villa’s defenders are more than happy to lure Brugge’s first line of pressure forward but have not yet been able to find an incisive line-breaking pass.

Seyes and Virgili combine down the left in Brugge’s best attack so far, but Torres is able to head behind for a corner, which is not up to much.

Wan-Bissaka has taken up a very aggressive position down Villa’s right and he earns a free-kick in a promising position. McGinn spins in a delivery which is only partially cleared but Maatsen’s effort from the edge of the box is smothered.

Villa get their foot on the ball from the get-go, circulating the ball around the back, before Suzuki launches a long ball up to Wan-Bissaka. The ball is worked to McGinn who feeds Buendia on the edge of the box but his effort flies just wide.

There is a minute’s silence for those affected by the floods in Nepal which is impeccably observed.

The players then retreat to their halves and Jackson gets us going!

Brugge and Villa emerge from the tunnel to the Champions League anthem... Here is this season’s introductory VT to whet the appetite.

The Champions League is back. #UCL pic.twitter.com/bsFGV69KMP

"This is a good test and challenge for us today." 💪Aston Villa boss Unai Emery looks ahead to their Champions League clash with Club Brugge.🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h4NF1jmiW6

As the rain lashes down in Bruges, you get the sense that Villa will have to dig deep to get a result and breathe life into their season. Both teams thrive on attacking transitions and the surface-level moisture will encourage breakaway moves.

Opta’s supercomputer has worked its magic again this season and placed Villa as the 10th favourites to lift the Champions League trophy. Back-to-back winners Paris St-Germain are only fifth. Here are the leading contenders before a ball has been kicked.

Agree? Leave your thoughts in the comments section beneath this live blog...

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

Club Brugge Sommer; Sabbe, Lee, Mechele, Seys; Potts, Vanaken; Forbs, Vetlesen, Virgili; Tresoldi

Substitutes Audoor, Coulibaly, Diakhon, Jackers, Lemarechal, Mike, Siquet, Spileers, Tsawa, Vanden Driessche, Vasovic, Vermant

Aston Villa Suzuki; Wan-Bissaka, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Hemmings; Jackson

Substitutes Abraham, Barkley, Bizot, Bogarde, Garnacho, Mbaye, Mings, Ruggeri, Wright, Alysson

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

Our ground crew for tonight. 👥📃 pic.twitter.com/UB7FUi9ZDH

Emery makes three changes from the XI that started against Hull City. Wan-Bissaka comes in for Matty Cash who does not make the match-day squad. Joao Gomes is eligible to play despite being suspended in domestic competition while Pau Torres replaces Tyrone Mings.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#2109. Reason for unexplained absence becomes clear as serious injury revealed | West Ham News

West Ham have, thankfully, avoided some of the problems which competing clubs have endured with huge swathes of first team players injured. Cardiff City struggled with eight players injured before the West Ham tie, but it didn’t stop the Bluebirds racing into a three goal lead and almost inflicting what would, in view of their first team being ‘decimated’, have been a humiliating defeat on their visitors.

By comparison, the Hammers have largely escaped such wholesale problems. Manor Solomon’s back problem and Kyle Walker Peters’ muscle issue seemed to be the main worries until sportwitness.co.uk revealed another squad injury that had been flying largely under the radar:

“West Ham United‘s Keiber Lamadrid went under the knife to resolve the physical problems that hampered his growth and development in England….During pre-season, he again suffered a knee injury in the friendly against 1. FC Magdeburg. There were concerns about a serious setback, but he returned to the pitch in August.

Lamadrid hasn’t featured for West Ham – now we know why

The player hasn’t made it to the match day squad since mid-September. Meridiano [news outlet] in Venezuela now states that this is because of fitness concerns, which have bothered him since moving to England.

Keiber Lamadrid has ‘put an end to the series of physical problems’ that stopped him from enjoying regular minutes with the Hammers. He did this by undergoing knee surgery.”

An interesting take on Lamadrid’s absence from match day squads.

It had been assumed that he was simply not impressing Nuno in training but the reveal that he’s been dealing with a long standing knee problem might well offer optimism that there’s a lot more to come from the young midfielder-slash-winger when he’s fully recuperated.

#2108. West Ham’s Home Advantage Problem Won’t Disappear With 60,000 Fans

Mark Noble has called on West Ham United supporters to help transform the London Stadium into an intimidating venue as Scott Parker prepares for his first home match in charge against Preston North End.

Speaking in an interview with the club’s official website, Noble praised the ‘extraordinary’ loyalty of West Ham fans following relegation and insisted that the club’s ambition remains an immediate return to the Premier League.

He also challenged supporters to make life uncomfortable for visiting teams, arguing that a crowd of 60,000 should give West Ham a significant advantage. But I think it’s important to point out that getting the fans onside and creating an intimidating atmosphere are probably two very different things.

There’s no doubt about it. When the London Stadium is loud, it is impressive, as anybody who attended that incredible night against Sevilla will testify.

But I do think it’s a long way from being intimidating.

For that to happen, I firmly believe supporters need to be close to the pitch.

Not just to cause opposition players discomfort, but to put pressure on referees and give West Ham the kind of home advantage that seems prevalent throughout the league.

The distance between the stands and the playing surface remains a fundamental problem, regardless of how many supporters are in attendance.

It’s something I’ve previously argued when discussing proposals to improve the stadium atmosphere.

Isolated tiers in the stadium and poor pitch proximity do little to help the atmosphere at the London Stadium

It was always my concern that relegation to the Championship would see visiting teams regard a trip to the London Stadium as a lovely day out in opulent surroundings. Opposition changing rooms are grand and palatial and their team coach can pull into the venue untroubled by home fans.

And our results in Stratford have certainly done little to disprove that theory. However, that doesn’t mean things can’t improve.

I genuinely believe that getting West Ham playing on the front foot will help eliminate some of the eerie silences we’ve heard so frequently at the London Stadium.

Noble wants supporters to see a team giving everything, and I think he’s absolutely right about that.

If Parker can produce an aggressive, attacking side that gives the crowd something to get excited about, the atmosphere should improve considerably.

But turning the London Stadium into a genuinely intimidating venue is another matter entirely.

And unfortunately, that’s a problem which can’t be solved simply by asking 60,000 people to make more noise.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Looking at all of the top games on TV, the stadia are considerably worse than London Stadium for proximity of fans.

Maybe we just lack the pyrotechnics in the crowd. The mad grabbing and jostling of inferior beings next to us. The joy of trying to intimidate anyone. We also lack a car park to show off our loutish best.

Whatever you think of the stadium, great and intimidating atmospheres can be choreographed to deliver at kick off, but if the team start sluggishly and without energy then that atmosphere will quickly deflate.

We were famously close to the pitch at Upton Park and won nothing for decades.

Blaming the stadium is just a distraction from the fact that we’re not playing well; when Andy Carroll scored that overhead kick against Palace, no one near me said they didn’t appreciate because they weren’t closer to the pitch.

If the ‘quality’ of the stadium is so important, explain Spurs to me…

#2107. Revealed : Parker tears up the Nuno rule book in Rush Green revolution | West Ham News

Training ground videos from the Nuno Espírito Santo era usually featured someone else taking training sessions at Rush Green: The former Hammers boss was usually nowhere to be seen when the customary pre-game PR videos were released with one of his assistants running the session.

His preparation was also rumoured to be perfunctory with short, superficial pre-match meetings, none of which produced the results on the pitch that would have helped him keep his job and West Ham keep their Premier League status.

As revealed by Roshane Thomas, writing in the NYTimes:

“Under Nuno, training lacked intensity and largely focused on small-sided games and running. Pre-match team meetings are said to have lasted 10 minutes on average and lacked detail…

Nuno Espirito Santo’s training sessions criticised today in revealing new report

During the international break, he [Scott Parker] has focused on high-intensity training. It has been his preferred approach, rather than team bonding exercises away from their training hub in Rush Green.

The players, however, have noticed a big difference under Parker. With help from assistant coaches Mark Noble, Jonathan Hill, Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Billy Lepine, Parker has prioritised working on pressing structure and shape with and without the ball.”

Which begs the question “Just what were the squad working on under Nuno”?

According to their new Manager, the changes he’s made have kicked in and there’s been a noticeable upturn. Which, lets face it, was long overdue, and after the new head coach’s first two games in charge was clearly, sorely needed.

“My general feeling is this is a group that are desperate to do well and work hard,” said Parker. “I’ve sensed that in the training sessions and what we’ve been doing. It’s still early days, I understand that, but there’s been some real improvement over the last two weeks”

We’ll all see for ourselves tomorrow when Preston North End visit: After his tough two-game baptism of fire, Parker got his two week break to prepare for a home tie against the bottom side. Which is as easy as it’s going to get this season.

#2106. Family's fury as 'elite' athlete twin brothers are arrested by ICE while on their way to college in Alabama

Published: 20:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 21:42 EST, 14 November 2026

A dismayed mother and father spoke out after their 'elite' athlete twin sons were arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as they returned to their Alabama college.

Wallace State Community College soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, 19, were taken into ICE custody after a traffic stop on November 4 while on their way to campus, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.

The Venezuelan twins were returning from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta, in Georgia when they were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer during a traffic stop in east-central Alabama.

The brothers graduated from Lawrenceville's Archer High School after a successful varsity soccer career that included a first ever region title for the school.

'This is the house of two elite soccer players,' Carlos Enrique Orta, their father, told the outlet.

Luis and Carlos are asylum seekers who applied for protections after legally entering the US on a tourist visa, like their parents.

That visa expired and the twins were granted US work permits and Georgia driver's licenses, according to the outlet.

A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, told the Daily Mail on Saturday that the brothers had legally entered the US with permission to stay on a temporary basis on June 21, 2022, but then 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws.'

Twin brothers and soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, both 19, were taken into ICE custody on November 5 after being arrested the previous day

Luis and Carlos were region title-winning soccer players for Archer High School in Lawrenceville, Georgia

The brothers were arrested as they returned from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta (both left)

The DHS spokesperson told the Daily Mail: 'All their claims will be heard by an immigration judge, and they will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law.'

'To be clear, pending applications do NOT confer legal status,' the statement continued.

Carlos was named the offensive player of the year and Luis the midfield player of the year by their high school this year.

They had received soccer scholarships to attend Wallace State, which they began doing this fall, but now face deportation to Venezuela.

'It's been hell,' Santoro de Orta, their mother, told the outlet.

She added that she supported ICE 'taking away the criminals' but said her children did not fit that description.

A final decision on the brothers' asylum case is still pending as they remain in custody.

The concerned mother claimed police said the twins' car had failed to come to a complete stop at a stop sign.

The brothers were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer as they were returning to Wallace State Community College, where they have soccer scholarships

The family applied for asylum protections after legally entering the country on a tourist visa. The DHS said the brothers 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws'

The Lincoln Police Department signed a partnership agreement with ICE in July.

ICE said the program allows trained local officers to exercise limited immigration authority during routine police work under federal supervision, according to the Cullman Tribune.

Luis and Carlos were booked into the Talladega County Jail on November 4 and transferred to ICE custody the following day.

Their father, Orta, described how the family was grappling with guilt as they shared what happened to their children.

'If anyone is at fault, it's me. It's us,' Orta told the outlet. 'Because I insist and I will continue to insist that Carlos and Luis came here because of a decision we made.'

He added: 'Carlos and Luis stayed here because of a decision from mom and dad. Carlos and Luis are here because of us.'

The Santoro twins were taken to the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana after their arrest, WABE reported.

The brothers have been taken to the the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana

The Lincoln Police Department signed an partnership agreement with ICE in July. A department officer arrested the brothers

A friend of the twins, Nicolas Azcarate Florez, said he had spoken to them multiple times since they were taken into custody.

'They've been saying that they've been moved five times, so it has been difficult for them,' Azcarate Florez told the outlet.

Azcarate Florez said the brothers were 'players that you could just give the ball to, and you would know that they would do something good with it.'

'If we needed them, we would know that they would be there to help us out of a sticky situation,' he added.

The brothers were taken into custody on the same week that the Republican Party faced a historic blue wave in the midterm elections that was seen as a rebuke of the GOP's immigration policy.

One of President Donald Trump's first moves afterwards was to name Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

Miller, one of Trump's most loyal and longest-serving advisers going back to his first administration, is known for his hardline views on immigration.

Critics have cited Miller as the architect of some of Trump's most divisive policies, including separating migrant families during deportations in the President's first term.

West Ham’s veteran midfielder has been the subject of an honest interview in his home country on Czech radio coinciding with the release of his autobiography. One of the more revealing comments Tomas Soucek made concerns the pressure and the expectation of playing in front of a big audience – such as West Ham will undoubtedly face tomorrow as the season re-commences with a home tie at London Stadium in front of 60,000 expectant supporters.

Unlike several others, from his words it is clear that Soucek seems to thrive on the pressure and the weight of expectation upon him. As one of only a handful of medal winners still at the club from the 2023 campaign, Soucek’s experience should become a steadying influence in the dressing room even though he mostly starts games on the bench these days.

Handling the weight of expectation at London Stadium has been daunting at times

“Yes, obviously I feel it, but I like the pressure. Because football is always up and down, you have so many wins and so many losses – and it’s up to you how you recover from all of it.

“And I love that. As you said, it’s the most watched league in the world. And West Ham’s fans are crazy – they’re the best in the league, and it’s such a historic club.

“From the first day until now, I think me and West Ham connection is as good as it could possibly be in all aspects.

“And, yes, the pressure is there, but I try to work with it – and that’s why we play football.” (englishradio.cz)

#2101. On The Road: Overpowered by County, but Accies are making small steps in the long road back from the abyss

Published: 08:28 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 10:25 EST, 15 November 2026

The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving New Douglas Park.

The decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe. There may, however, be a positive prognosis.

Accies, despite their defeat, are whispering about stability, even though ‘legacy debt’ has to be faced, perhaps contested.

County, meanwhile, will not say it even in a whisper but Saturday’s victory takes them eight points clear at the top and heavily fancied for the title. The Staggies have one set of hooves in the Championship.

Scottish football, of course, does not restrict itself to the cliched fare of top of the table clashes so New Douglas Park hosted a striker who is 39 later this month, a winger who was once a Scottish international, and a gentleman in the stands who once played against George Best. And a Ross County fan who regularly travels up from North Wales.

These exotic avenues demand to be explored but perennial questions about the financial health of the Accies had to be asked, too, after reports this week stating that hospitality packages at the club were being suspended.

An Accies fan feels the pain of defeat during Saturday's home loss to Ross County

Allan Currie, chairman, answered them over a half-time pie.

‘We have come on in leaps and bounds but every week seems to throw up different challenges,’ he said. ‘We have a level of debt that we have inherited and we are working with the creditors to try to navigate our way through that.’

Matters on the field are positive, despite Saturday’s defeat.

‘The guys on the pitch, manager, and his staff have been unbelievable. Surviving in this league last season was phenomenal given what they were going through but it couldn’t be better now,’ he said. ‘Off the pitch, we are fighting with the different challenges we have. We are in a much better place even if we are not out the woods yet.’

Asked what the level of pressure on him, he said: ‘I am the guy on the ground but Rob Edwards is carrying out negotiations.’

Edwards, through his Morley Group, took over the club earlier this year but has been sideswiped by a number of claims for payment. However, Currie has faith in the owner.

‘Without him, the club would not survive. Rob should take all the credit,’ he said.

Asked what the short-term aims for the club were, Currie replied with a smile: ‘A goal in the second half would be good.’ A goal was scored but not for the Accies.

But the club remain in second place and the play-offs seem a more than reasonable prospect.

Ross County goalscorer Kieran Phillips battles with Hamilton's Kai Smutek

With 10 minutes to go, Hamilton brought on their latest signing. Barrie McKay, who has played for Scotland and scored for Rangers in a Scottish Cup semi-final against Celtic. His considerable achievements, though, paled in comparison to the subject of a casual conversation in the bar before the match.

‘I played against George Best,’ said Alan McDougall, with an air so off-hand one could have believed he was merely ordering another pint.

‘Yes, I played 200 games for the Accies. Davie McParland brought me here as a 21-year-old and I played for about six years. I went to Stranraer for a year and then went down south. I played against Best with the Accies.’

The Northern Irish genius played for Hibernian in 1979-80. ‘He was well past his best and that was sad,’ said McDougall. Best’s addiction to alcohol had taken a severe toll.

‘I came back to watch games five or six years ago,’ said McDougall. ‘When the club went to Clyde, it destroyed me. What is fantastic is that the people that are now in control seem to be turning it around.’

There was a mood of cautious optimism from other fans. ‘I have been a fan since forever, well the 1980s at least,’ said Gavin Fullarton. ‘I have seen this team in every division. I have seen them in the downs and downs. But I think we are going in the right direction. So far.’

He added: ‘The new guys seem to know what they are doing. They are communicative.’

There were 1,216 fans in the ground on Saturday with 300 stalwarts travelling down from the north. Colin Richardson, an Accies supporter, was asked why so many had stuck by the club.

‘It’s about loyalty,’ he said. ‘You can’t pick and choose when you support your team. At the moment it is all about small steps. It has to be about stability.’

A Ross County fan had travelled up from North Wales. The journey to Scotland is a familiar one for Ian Ellson. ‘I have been all over Scotland to watch Ross County,’ he said. ‘Twenty years ago I visited Ross County and I was spoiled rotten. I decided to follow them.’

A social worker, he averages one visit a month. ‘I live and breathe Ross County,’ he said. ‘This season we are going up.’

Welsh Staggies fan Ian Elson and Englishman Ray Griffiths travelled far for Saturday's game

Brian Graham would not be so bullish. He is 39 this month and has learned enough about football to know that predictions are made only to make the speaker seem foolish down the line.

He was, though, expansive about what is happening at County. He joined the club for the second time in the summer after Stuart Kettlewell, the manager, convinced him of the ambitions in Dingwall.

‘This is a club where I have had success before so I know how good a club it can be,’ he said. ‘It’s not been great for a couple of seasons but in the summer the manager set out his stall very early. It was about leaving egos at the door, building a togetherness and having a change of culture at the club. I think you are seeing that now.’

The early signs were good for the striker who dropped down from Falkirk in the Premiership to play in Dingwall.

‘We had good pre-season performances against Aberdeen and Dundee and that was a solid building block,’ he said.

Brian Graham celebrates after scoring his 21st goal of the season for County

Graham converted a first-half penalty to reach a tally of 21 goals this season and the Christmas trees are not up yet. ‘I get a lot of plaudits for scoring goals but others in the team are scoring a lot too,’ he said. ‘We are scoring team goals.’

Has he set a target for the season? ‘When I came back I knew I had to score 13 to reach 50 goals for the club in two spells,’ he said. ‘I always set down targets in a wee black book but now I might need to readjust that.’

It was a night of adjustment for Darian MacKinnon. He had set a victory target but was condemned to accept defeat. He would not concede the league race was over. ‘We have to play them twice,’ he said.

He added ‘We are going in the right direction. The owners have put money in and they have backed us.’

Asked to pinpoint a factor that has contributed to the team sitting second, he said: ‘The most positive thing for me this season is that this is now a good place to come into your work after the last three or four seasons. We are all actually enjoying coming to our work.’

There is work to be done on and off the pitch but the Accies are surviving. And that is the biggest result.

#2100. Sonia Bompastor's side show their teeth as Chelsea sink the reigning champions to reclaim top spot in WSL title race: Chelsea 1-0 Man City

By SAMARA WATTS and TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 10:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 11:33 EST, 15 November 2026

Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.

Sandy Baltimore's first-half goal was enough to ensure Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blow the title race wide open.

After keeping the reigning WSL champions at bay following an early barrage, Chelsea grew in confidence but still lacked the cutting edge that had seen them held to back-to-back draws in the past week.

A moment of magic from Baltimore in the fourth minute of stoppage time ensured history would not repeat itself.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson, a move which appeared to invigorate the visitors, but Chelsea held firm to pick up all three points.

Daily Mail Sport's Tara Anson-Walsh and Samara Watts were at Stamford Bridge to bring you the things we learned...

Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blew the title race wide open

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson

Devastation for Kadeisha Buchanan, who was hooked after 11 minutes by Bompastor. The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match as she looked out of her depth against Bunny Shaw, ever a precarious place to be against the league’s top striker.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor said.

'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'

For those sceptical, it certainly improved things.

The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match and was hooked after just 11 minutes

Women’s football royalty Sarina Wiegman and Emma Hayes braved the chilly climes of Stamford Bridge to witness the showdown between the WSL heavyweights on Saturday afternoon.

The freshly anointed honorary Dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes and the pair chatted warmly, with Wiegman laughing as Hayes attempted to encourage her to celebrate Chelsea's victory at full time. This is a relationship that will no doubt drop in cordiality as the sand in the hourglass ahead of next summer’s World Cup continues to run down.

Wiegman had several England players on her watching brief, not least young Lexi Potter, whose stock has risen dramatically this season. The 20-year-old put in another assured performance against the reigning champions, continuing to demonstrate her maturity in the highest stakes, which will no doubt put her in a good position ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement.

Elsewhere, the Dutch coach will have been alarmed by the number of crunching tackles put in against her right back, Lucy Bronze, in this match. If there is one player that she will want to wrap up in cotton wool ahead of Brazil, it is the recently turned 35-year-old Bronze for her steadfast leadership and relentless athleticism.

One player looking to make an impact ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement was Aggie Beever-Jones, who has struggled this season and was left out of Sonia Bompastor’s starting line-up. An injury to Melvine Malard saw Beever-Jones gain more minutes than she would have expected, but it felt like another afternoon of deja vu for the 23-year-old forward as she failed to convert a number of chances despite finding herself in good positions.

Meanwhile, in Manchester, Ella Toone's hopes of forcing her way back into Sarina Wiegman's plans suffered another blow as the 27-year-old was once again left out of Eva Olid's starting line-up for United's 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. Toone watched on as fellow Lioness Maya Le Tissier opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike, and the two-time European champion will no doubt be growing increasingly concerned as Brazil draws closer.

The freshly anointed honorary dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes at the WSL showpiece at Stamford Bridge and the pair chatted warmly

Melvine Malard’s absence raises questions about who Chelsea’s main goalscorer will be this season. The squad has lacked a clinical edge without England striker Lauren James, who is out with a hamstring injury until the international break.

The French forward went off injured after 35 minutes with a suspected hamstring injury. Although she missed Chelsea’s opening games after picking up a knock in pre-season, she has been the Blues’ top scorer in the absence of Lauren James with six league goals so far.

Chelsea are averaging 24 shots per game, an unprecedented rate across a WSL campaign, but have recently struggled to convert their chances. They were held to a 0-0 draw against BK Hacken midweek in the UWCL and a 1-1 draw against Everton last weekend.

Malard leaving the pitch meant Chelsea struggled to find a creative spark up front. Her replacement Aggie Beever-Jones has been dealing with an ankle injury, and is still trying to find her feet with only one goal in the WSL.

Head coach Bompastor said: ‘The frustration sometimes comes from us not being ruthless and clinical.’

A moment of magic from Malard’s French international teammate Sandy Baltimore was enough to make it 1-0 just before half time with the team’s first shot on target. However, Baltimore was substituted at half time to manage her minutes, and Chelsea were unable to capitalize on any of their chances in the second half.

Bompastor said: ‘From the outside it seems like we have had a lot of injuries, but we have been playing every three days.’

‘I knew coming into the game we were not as fresh as we would like to be, but that’s our environment.

‘We want to play in every competition but the players are not robots,’

Melvine Malard’s injury could cause more problems for the Blues’ attack, as they registered just two shots on target today and scraped the three points.

Malard limped off in the first half and meant Chelsea struggled for a creative spark up front

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box and took down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal in the 75th minute.

The Blues were mounting a rapid attack down the left hand side, with Thompson just outside the box when Yamashita missed the ball and brought her to the ground.

The Japanese goalkeeper was shown a straight red card and was sent off the pitch. This was City’s first red card in the WSL since November 2023, and a rare moment of madness from the usually-composed 31-year-old.

The referee allowed City three minutes to replace the Japanese goalkeeper, with Scotland’s number one Eartha Cumings coming on to replace forward Aoba Fujino.

Her first test arrived only a minute later, as Aggie Beever-Jones' right-footed shot from the resulting indirect free kick dropped dangerously, but she was saved by the crossbar.

The bigger question now is whether Yamashita's absence - which could amass to three games - will have a lasting impact on their title race.

In the short-term against Chelsea, City reacted well. Andree Jeglertz said at full time: ‘The players dealt with it in a good way, so even though we were one player down we had a couple of great opportunities to score a goal. Of course it affected the game but that is not why we lost.’

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as Manchester City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box to take down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal

Chelsea’s win at the Bridge blows the title race wide open, as they are now just one point ahead of City at the top of the WSL table.

Bompastor’s side ended City’s unbeaten streak, and they now have 24 league goals compared to City’s 16 after 10 games.

However, with seven shots and just one on target this game, Chelsea will need to look at their attacking options as they take on Liverpool and London City Lionesses before the international break.

Bompastor said: ‘It’s a nice feeling to be top of the table right now and to win against these top sides, but I know we still have a lot of work to be done and it’s early on in the season so many things can happen.’

City were unable to create opportunities in front of goal, with the WSL’s all-time leading goalscorer Vivianne Miedema’s return overshadowed by Ayaka Yamashita’s nightmare in goal.

City head coach Andree Jeglertz said: ‘They managed to score on their big chance and (it was a) great finish.

'We also had some great opportunities where we didn’t manage to score, but I think we deserve more than going away from here with no points.’

London City Lionesses face Arsenal tomorrow at the Emirates, and a win in north London could bring them four points behind the new WSL leaders, and really start to make things interesting.
